newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile 2nd-half growth seen near 6.5 pct - minister.
newsitem.headline: Chile 2nd-half growth seen near 6.5 pct - minister.

text.p: The Chilean central bank's decision to cut interest rates should enable the economy to return to growth of about 6.5 percent in the second half of the year, Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia said on Thursday.
"I see no reason for the Chilean economy not to resume a pace of growth of about 6.5 percent," Garcia said at the National Chamber of Commerce.
Late Thursday, the central bank said it was cutting the interbank borrowing rate by 25 basis points to 6.75 percent annual.

The long-expected move came after official government data showed sluggish growth in the first quarter. It also reflected the government's success in bringing down inflation, which in May stood at a mere 0.2 percent.
"All these elements backed up the reduction of rates by the central bank," said Garcia.
On an annualized basis, May consumer inflation was 5.4 percent, which suggested the central bank's goal of 5.5 percent inflation in 1997 was achievable, officials said.
